title: Deep Demonstration Tracing: Learning Generalizable Imitator Policy for Runtime Imitation from a Single Demonstration

en.text: One-shot imitation learning (OSIL) asks an agent to carry out a task after watching a single demonstration. It works remarkably well when the deployment environment looks like the one where the demonstration was recorded. The trouble is that the real world rarely holds still. After a route is demonstrated, a truck can park across the path; after a grasp is shown, the object can slip out of the gripper. These are exactly the moments where a demonstration stops being a script to replay and becomes, at best, a rough guide.

Most OSIL methods embed the demonstration as a context vector and clone the demonstrated actions. In a stationary world that is enough. But once an unforeseen change pushes the agent into a state the demonstration never covered, blind replay has nothing sensible to say - and existing methods degrade sharply. This paper, presented at ICML 2024, takes that failure mode as its subject.

The authors' answer is Deep Demonstration Tracing (DDT): instead of replaying a demonstration, the agent learns to trace it. It figures out which demonstrated states are relevant right now, reads off how the expert behaved there, and steers back onto the demonstrated path after a detour. DDT pairs a purpose-built demonstration transformer with a meta-reinforcement-learning training scheme, and it holds up where prior one-shot imitation methods collapse.

en.caption: Figure 1. A pick-and-place task in Meta-World where the object slips mid-execution. Given the demonstration (a), a traditional OSIL policy (b) drops the object and fails, while the DDT policy (c) re-picks the object and still succeeds - the difference between replaying actions and tracing intent.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05285   |   Code: https://github.com/xionghuichen/Deep-Demonstration-Tracing   |   Project page: https://osil-ddt.github.io
When replay is not enough

Formally, a task is a Markov decision process (MDP), and OSIL provides one expert trajectory as the only description of what the agent should do. Prior work has largely studied the setting where collection and deployment are near-identical, so a policy that reproduces the demonstrated action at each demonstrated state does fine. The paper deliberately widens the gap between collection and deployment - adding obstacles, disturbances, and other unforeseen changes at runtime - and shows that this is where the interesting difficulty lives, and where it has been under-studied.
The requirement, then, is not merely to match demonstrated actions but to behave sensibly off the demonstrated path and to find the way back. That is an adaptivity current methods do not build in.
A blueprint borrowed from human imitation

The design starts from how a person imitates a route. Following a demonstrated path toward a destination, you meet a truck parked where the demonstration had none. You do not freeze or restart; you detour around the obstacle and rejoin the original path at a convenient point. The authors distill this into a three-stage decision process: identify which demonstrated states are relevant to the current situation, analyze how the expert behaved in those states, and trace back onto the demonstration.

en.caption: Figure 2. The human blueprint for one-shot imitation under unforeseen change. The expert trajectory (dashed) runs from start S to target P; a truck (absent when the demonstration was collected) blocks state B. A capable imitator leaves the demonstrated path, detours (green), and rejoins the demonstration - identify, analyze, then trace back.

en.text: This blueprint is not just narrative color: it becomes the literal structure of the network. Each of the three stages maps onto a specific computation in the demonstration transformer, which is what turns an intuition about human behavior into an inductive bias the model can learn with.
The demonstration transformer

The core module treats the agent's current state as a query and the demonstration's state-action pairs as keys and values. An attention-weighting module scores which demonstrated states matter now (identify). A point-wise multiplication then combines those weights with the encoded expert behavior to read off what the expert did there (analyze). The result is folded back together with the current state and passed through an MLP to produce the action (trace). The expert-state encoder and the visited-state encoder share weights, so demonstrated and current states are compared in the same representation space.

en.caption: Figure 3. The demonstration transformer. Reading bottom to top, the three human stages become network operations: attention weighting (Stage 1, identify which states to follow), point-wise multiplication (Stage 2, analyze how the expert behaved), and recombination with the current state through an MLP (Stage 3, trace back and act). The expert-state and visited-state encoders share weights.

en.text: Rolling the demonstration encoder and the context-based policy into a single architecture is what gives DDT its inductive bias toward tracing. That bias is also what lets it generalize to demonstrations - and to disturbances - it never saw during training, rather than memorizing a fixed mapping from context to action.
Training it as meta-RL, not behavior cloning

The second ingredient is how the policy is trained. Behavior cloning can only teach the agent what to do at states the demonstration visited, which is precisely the wrong tool when the whole problem is behaving well off the demonstrated path. DDT instead casts one-shot imitation as context-based meta-reinforcement learning: the demonstration is the context, and the agent learns by interaction to act even in states the demonstration never reached.

The reward is a stationary OSIL reward that combines a term rewarding the agent for following the demonstration with a large-weighted task reward that keeps the focus on actually completing the task. This dense signal is what makes learning efficient early on, and the whole objective is optimized with Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). The paper also gives a theoretical condition on the environment - roughly, that it is recoverable back onto the demonstration - under which one trajectory suffices for imitation.
VPAM: a benchmark built for unforeseen change

To test imitation under runtime change, the authors build Valet Parking Assist in Maze (VPAM), inspired by real-world valet parking. A point agent must travel from a start to a target in a maze it has never seen globally, relying only on short local views computed from eight rays over five steps. Crucially, rectangular obstacles are randomly placed on the route and often did not exist in the demonstration, so the agent cannot simply replay demonstrated actions. Eight task variants toggle whether it is a single map or many, whether obstacles appear, and whether the agent is told its own coordinates.

en.caption: Figure 4. A VPAM maze. The agent moves from the start (blue) to the target (green) guided by the demonstration points (gray), while unexpected obstacles (brown) block the demonstrated route. The agent perceives only a small local view (shaded), and DDT's imitation trajectory (red) detours around each obstacle and rejoins the demonstration.

en.text: Beyond VPAM, DDT is also evaluated on robotics benchmarks: Meta-World with added disturbances, Gymnasium's Reacher and Pusher, and a MuJoCo manipulation task involving grasping, stacking, and clutter, along with partially observable variants of the VPAM maze itself.
How well does it hold up?

On VPAM, DDT leads across every setting - and, more tellingly, it degrades far less as conditions get harder. Moving from the training distribution to non-obstacle test maps to unforeseen obstacles, DDT drops only from 0.86 to 0.84 to 0.73, a 15% fall. The baselines fall 20%, 33%, and 52% over the same span, so DDT retains at least 5% more of its performance than any competitor.

en.caption: Figure 5. Success rates on VPAM across three settings. DDT (red) leads DCRL, CbMRL, and the behavior-cloning Trans4OSIL in every setting, and the gap widens under unforeseen obstacles - where DDT reaches 0.73 against the best baseline's 0.57. Black bars show standard error across tasks over three seeds.
Table 1. VPAM success rates (higher is better) and degradation from Train to the Unforeseen-Obstacle setting.

en.text: The robotics results tell the same story more starkly. On Meta-World with disturbance, DDT succeeds 61% of the time on unseen demonstrations, whereas the strongest baseline manages at most about 12%. The meta-RL mechanism, not just the transformer, is what buys this robustness to change.
Is it really tracing?

A method named for tracing should be shown to trace. The authors visualize a DDT rollout in a maze together with the attention scores the demonstration transformer places over the expert trajectory as the agent moves. If DDT were following the demonstration, the attention should shift along the expert path roughly in step with the agent's own progress.

en.caption: Figure 7. Left: a trajectory generated by DDT, detouring around obstacles and returning to the demonstrated route. Right: the attention score map, agent step (vertical) against expert step (horizontal). The bright band runs down the diagonal - as the agent advances, its attention tracks the corresponding part of the demonstration, which is tracing made visible.

en.text: That diagonal is the mechanism working as intended: attention follows the demonstration in step with the agent, breaking away exactly when a detour is needed and re-locking afterward. It is a satisfying check that the architecture is doing the thing its design was meant to encourage.
Ablations and scaling

Two ablations confirm that both ingredients matter. Swapping the demonstration transformer for a standard transformer noticeably lowers asymptotic performance - so it is the tailored architecture, not attention in general, that drives the imitation ability. Removing the OSIL reward and learning only from the sparse ending reward sharply slows learning, because the OSIL reward supplies the dense signal that lets the agent follow the demonstration early in training.

en.caption: Figure 8. Left: learning curves (success rate vs. environment steps) for DDT and its ablations; replacing the demonstration transformer or dropping the OSIL reward both hurt. Right: asymptotic success rate as data and model size scale up (log x-axis) - performance climbs log-linearly, with roughly a 2x gain from scaling model parameters.

en.text: The scaling curves are a quieter but intriguing result: DDT improves log-linearly with both data volume and model size, roughly doubling as parameters grow. That clean scaling behavior is what leads the authors to suggest DDT could serve as a backbone for larger, more general decision-making agents.
Takeaway

The core idea is small and durable: an agent handed a single demonstration should learn to trace it, not replay it - identifying which demonstrated states are relevant now, reading off what the expert did, and steering back onto the path after a detour. DDT operationalizes this with a demonstration transformer trained by meta-RL, and the payoff is one-shot imitation that stays robust when the environment changes at runtime, a regime where earlier methods fail.

The honest boundaries are worth keeping in view: the single-demonstration guarantee rests on a recoverability condition, and the headline results live on a purpose-built maze benchmark alongside a set of robotics tasks. Within that scope, though, DDT is a clean demonstration that the right inductive bias plus reinforcement learning beats behavior cloning when the world refuses to stay still - and its scaling behavior hints at more to come.

zh.text: 单样本模仿学习(One-shot Imitation Learning,OSIL)要求智能体只看一条示范,就把任务完成。在部署环境与采集示范时几乎一致的情况下,这类方法表现相当好。问题在于,真实世界很少一成不变:路线示范给出之后,可能突然有辆卡车停在路中间;抓取动作演示完,物体也可能从夹爪里滑落。正是在这些时刻,示范不再是一份可以逐步照抄的脚本,顶多只能算一份粗略的向导。
大多数 OSIL 方法把示范编码成一个上下文向量,然后克隆示范中的动作。在静态环境里这已经够用。可一旦出现未曾预料的变化,把智能体推入示范从未覆盖的状态,盲目照抄就无从应对,已有方法的性能也会急剧下滑。这篇发表于 ICML 2024 的工作,正是把这一失效模式当作研究对象。
作者给出的答案是 Deep Demonstration Tracing(DDT,深度示范追踪):与其照抄示范,不如学会“追踪”示范——先判断当前时刻哪些示范状态是相关的,再读出专家在那些状态下的行为,最后在绕行之后重新回到示范的路径上。DDT 把一个专门设计的示范 Transformer 与元强化学习(meta-RL)训练方案结合起来,在以往单样本模仿方法失效的地方依然站得住脚。

zh.caption: 图1 展示 Meta-World 中的一个抓取-放置任务,物体在执行中途滑落。面对同一条示范(a),传统 OSIL 策略(b)掉落物体后直接失败,而 DDT 策略(c)重新抓取物体并最终成功——这正是“照抄动作”与“追踪意图”的差别。

zh.text: 论文:https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05285   |   代码:https://github.com/xionghuichen/Deep-Demonstration-Tracing   |   项目主页:https://osil-ddt.github.io
当“照抄”不再奏效
从形式上看,一个任务就是一个马尔可夫决策过程(MDP),而 OSIL 只提供一条专家轨迹作为“该做什么”的唯一描述。以往工作大多研究采集与部署几乎一致的设定,此时只要在每个示范状态复现示范动作,策略就能应付。本文则刻意拉大采集与部署之间的差距——在运行时加入障碍、扰动等未曾预料的变化——并指出真正有意思、也长期被忽视的难点恰恰在这里。
于是,要求就不再只是复现示范动作,而是要在偏离示范的状态下也能做出合理行为,并找到回到示范的路。这正是现有方法没有内建的自适应能力。
来自人类模仿的蓝本
方法的设计起点,是人类如何模仿一条路线。沿着示范路线走向目的地时,你遇到一辆停在原本没有障碍处的卡车。你不会僵住,也不会重头再来,而是绕过障碍,再在合适的地方重新汇入原路线。作者把这一过程提炼成一个三阶段决策流程:识别(identify)当前情境下哪些示范状态相关,分析(analyze)专家在这些状态下如何行动,再追踪(trace)回到示范之上。

zh.caption: 图2 未预料变化下单样本模仿的人类蓝本。专家轨迹(虚线)从起点 S 通向目标 P;一辆采集示范时并不存在的卡车挡住了状态 B。合格的模仿者会离开示范路径、绕行(绿色),再重新汇入示范——先识别、再分析、最后追踪回去。

zh.text: 这套蓝本不只是叙事上的点缀,它会直接变成网络的结构:三个阶段各自对应示范 Transformer 中一项具体运算。正是这种对应关系,把关于人类行为的直觉转化成模型可以学习的归纳偏置。
示范 Transformer

核心模块把智能体当前状态作为查询(query),把示范的状态-动作对作为键(key)与值(value)。注意力加权模块为“当前哪些示范状态重要”打分,对应识别阶段;随后的逐点相乘(point-wise multiplication)把这些权重与编码后的专家行为结合,读出专家在那些状态下做了什么,对应分析阶段;结果再与当前状态重新融合,经一个 MLP 输出动作,对应追踪阶段。专家状态编码器与已访状态编码器共享权重,使示范状态与当前状态在同一表示空间中比较。

zh.caption: 图3 示范 Transformer。自下而上,人类的三个阶段被落实为网络运算:注意力加权(阶段一,识别该跟随哪些状态)、逐点相乘(阶段二,分析专家如何行动),以及与当前状态重新融合后经 MLP 输出动作(阶段三,追踪回去并行动)。专家状态编码器与已访状态编码器共享权重。

zh.text: 把示范编码器与基于上下文的策略整合进同一个架构,正是 DDT 倾向“追踪”的归纳偏置来源。也正是这种偏置,让它能够泛化到训练中从未见过的示范与扰动,而不是死记一套从上下文到动作的固定映射。
以元强化学习训练,而非行为克隆
第二个要素在于训练方式。行为克隆(behavior cloning)只能教会智能体在示范访问过的状态该做什么,而当整个问题恰恰是“在偏离示范的状态下也要表现良好”时,这正好用错了工具。DDT 转而把单样本模仿建模成基于上下文的元强化学习:示范作为上下文,智能体通过与环境交互,学会在示范从未到达的状态下也能行动。
奖励采用一种平稳的 OSIL 奖励,它把“鼓励智能体跟随示范”的项,与一个大权重的任务奖励结合起来,后者确保重心始终落在真正完成任务上。这个稠密信号让训练早期就能高效学习,整个目标用 Soft Actor-Critic(SAC)优化。论文还给出一个理论条件——大致是环境可从偏离处“恢复”回示范——在该条件下,单条轨迹就足以成功模仿。
VPAM:为“未预料变化”而生的基准

为了检验运行时变化下的模仿能力,作者构建了 VPAM(Valet Parking Assist in Maze,迷宫代客泊车),灵感来自现实中的代客泊车。一个质点智能体要在从未从全局见过的迷宫里,从起点走到目标,只能依靠由 8 条射线、5 步范围计算出的局部视野。关键在于,矩形障碍会随机出现在路线上,而它们往往在示范中并不存在,因此智能体无法简单照抄示范动作。八个任务变体分别切换:单张地图还是多张、是否出现障碍、以及是否提供坐标。

zh.caption: 图4 一张 VPAM 迷宫。智能体在示范点(灰色)引导下,从起点(蓝色)走向目标(绿色),而未预料的障碍(棕色)挡住了示范路线。智能体只能感知很小的局部视野(阴影区),DDT 的模仿轨迹(红色)绕过每个障碍后重新汇入示范。

zh.text: 除 VPAM 外,DDT 还在多个机器人基准上评测:带扰动的 Meta-World、Gymnasium 的 Reacher 与 Pusher,以及一个涉及抓取、堆叠与杂乱环境的 MuJoCo 操作任务,另有部分可观测的 VPAM 变体。
它到底有多稳?
在 VPAM 上,DDT 在每个设定下都领先;更说明问题的是,随着条件变难,它的下滑幅度小得多。从训练分布,到无障碍测试地图,再到未预料障碍,DDT 的成功率仅从 0.86 降到 0.84 再到 0.73,跌幅 15%。而基线在同一跨度上分别下滑 20%、33% 与 52%,也就是说 DDT 至少多保留了 5% 的性能。

zh.caption: 图5 VPAM 三种设定下的成功率。DDT(红)在每个设定下都领先 DCRL、CbMRL 以及行为克隆式的 Trans4OSIL,且在未预料障碍下差距进一步拉大——DDT 达到 0.73,而最强基线仅 0.57。黑色误差条为三个随机种子下各任务间的标准误。
表1 VPAM 成功率(越高越好),以及从训练集到未预料障碍设定的下滑幅度。

zh.text: 机器人实验把这个故事讲得更鲜明。在带扰动的 Meta-World 上,DDT 在未见过的示范上有 61% 的成功率,而最强基线最多也只有约 12%。带来这种对变化的稳健性的,是元强化学习机制,而不仅仅是 Transformer。
它真的在“追踪”吗?
一个以“追踪”命名的方法,理应证明它确实在追踪。作者把 DDT 在迷宫中的一次运行,与示范 Transformer 在智能体前进时对专家轨迹给出的注意力分数一并可视化。如果 DDT 确实在跟随示范,那么注意力应当大致随智能体自身的推进,沿着专家路径逐步移动。

zh.caption: 图7 左:DDT 生成的一条轨迹,绕过障碍后重新回到示范路线。右:注意力分数图,纵轴为智能体步数,横轴为专家步数。明亮的条带沿对角线延伸——智能体每前进一步,注意力就跟踪到示范的对应部分,这正是“追踪”的可视化。

zh.text: 那条对角线正是机制如预期般工作的证据:注意力随智能体同步跟随示范,恰在需要绕行时短暂偏离,绕行之后又重新锁定。这是一个令人安心的验证,说明架构确实在做它被设计去鼓励的那件事。
消融与规模化
两项消融确认了两个要素缺一不可。把示范 Transformer 换成标准 Transformer,渐近性能明显下降——可见起作用的是这套量身定制的架构,而非泛泛的注意力机制。去掉 OSIL 奖励、只用稀疏的结束奖励学习,则会显著拖慢学习,因为 OSIL 奖励提供的稠密信号,正是让智能体在训练早期就能紧跟示范的关键。

zh.caption: 图8 左:DDT 及其消融版本的学习曲线(成功率对环境步数);替换示范 Transformer 或去掉 OSIL 奖励都会带来损害。右:随数据量与模型规模扩大时的渐近成功率(横轴为对数)——性能呈对数线性上升,仅扩大模型参数就带来约 2x(两倍)的提升。

zh.text: 规模化曲线是一个更安静却引人兴趣的结果:DDT 随数据量与模型规模都呈对数线性提升,参数增大时成功率大致翻倍。正是这种干净的规模化行为,让作者提出 DDT 或可作为更大、更通用决策智能体的骨干网络。
小结
核心思想简单而经得起推敲:拿到一条示范的智能体,应当学会追踪它,而非照抄它——判断此刻哪些示范状态相关,读出专家做了什么,并在绕行之后重新回到路径上。DDT 用一个由元强化学习训练的示范 Transformer 把这一思想落地,回报是当环境在运行时发生变化时依然稳健的单样本模仿,而这恰是以往方法失效的区域。
也应看清它诚实的边界:单条示范的保证依赖一个可恢复性条件,而最亮眼的结果建立在一个专门构建的迷宫基准以及一组机器人任务之上。但在这一范围内,DDT 干净地表明了:当世界拒绝静止时,合适的归纳偏置加上强化学习,胜过行为克隆——而它的规模化表现,也让人对后续充满期待。

zh.text: 单样本模仿学习(One-shot Imitation Learning,OSIL)要求智能体只看一条示范,就把任务完成。在部署环境与采集示范时几乎一致的情况下,这类方法表现相当好。问题在于,真实世界很少一成不变:路线示范给出之后,可能突然有辆卡车停在路中间;抓取动作演示完,物体也可能从夹爪里滑落。正是在这些时刻,示范不再是一份可以逐步照抄的脚本,顶多只能算一份粗略的向导。
大多数 OSIL 方法把示范编码成一个上下文向量,然后克隆示范中的动作。在静态环境里这已经够用。可一旦出现未曾预料的变化,把智能体推入示范从未覆盖的状态,盲目照抄就无从应对,已有方法的性能也会急剧下滑。这篇发表于 ICML 2024 的工作,正是把这一失效模式当作研究对象。
作者给出的答案是 Deep Demonstration Tracing(DDT,深度示范追踪):与其照抄示范,不如学会“追踪”示范——先判断当前时刻哪些示范状态是相关的,再读出专家在那些状态下的行为,最后在绕行之后重新回到示范的路径上。DDT 把一个专门设计的示范 Transformer 与元强化学习(meta-RL)训练方案结合起来,在以往单样本模仿方法失效的地方依然站得住脚。

zh.subtitle: 南京大学与南栖仙策提出 Deep Demonstration Tracing(DDT):让单样本模仿在环境突变时依然稳健

en.caption: Figure 1. A pick-and-place task in Meta-World where the object slips mid-execution. Given the demonstration (a), a traditional OSIL policy (b) drops the object and fails, while the DDT policy (c) re-picks the object and still succeeds - the difference between replaying actions and tracing intent.

en.text: When replay is not enough

Formally, a task is a Markov decision process (MDP), and OSIL provides one expert trajectory as the only description of what the agent should do. Prior work has largely studied the setting where collection and deployment are near-identical, so a policy that reproduces the demonstrated action at each demonstrated state does fine. The paper deliberately widens the gap between collection and deployment - adding obstacles, disturbances, and other unforeseen changes at runtime - and shows that this is where the interesting difficulty lives, and where it has been under-studied.
The requirement, then, is not merely to match demonstrated actions but to behave sensibly off the demonstrated path and to find the way back. That is an adaptivity current methods do not build in.

zh.caption: 图1 展示 Meta-World 中的一个抓取-放置任务,物体在执行中途滑落。面对同一条示范(a),传统 OSIL 策略(b)掉落物体后直接失败,而 DDT 策略(c)重新抓取物体并最终成功——这正是“照抄动作”与“追踪意图”的差别。

zh.text: 当“照抄”不再奏效
从形式上看,一个任务就是一个马尔可夫决策过程(MDP),而 OSIL 只提供一条专家轨迹作为“该做什么”的唯一描述。以往工作大多研究采集与部署几乎一致的设定,此时只要在每个示范状态复现示范动作,策略就能应付。本文则刻意拉大采集与部署之间的差距——在运行时加入障碍、扰动等未曾预料的变化——并指出真正有意思、也长期被忽视的难点恰恰在这里。
于是,要求就不再只是复现示范动作,而是要在偏离示范的状态下也能做出合理行为,并找到回到示范的路。这正是现有方法没有内建的自适应能力。

zh.subtitle: 南京大学与南栖仙策提出 Deep Demonstration Tracing(DDT):让单样本模仿在环境突变时依然稳健

en.text: The demonstration transformer

The core module treats the agent's current state as a query and the demonstration's state-action pairs as keys and values. An attention-weighting module scores which demonstrated states matter now (identify). A point-wise multiplication then combines those weights with the encoded expert behavior to read off what the expert did there (analyze). The result is folded back together with the current state and passed through an MLP to produce the action (trace). The expert-state encoder and the visited-state encoder share weights, so demonstrated and current states are compared in the same representation space.

en.caption: Figure 3. The demonstration transformer. Reading bottom to top, the three human stages become network operations: attention weighting (Stage 1, identify which states to follow), point-wise multiplication (Stage 2, analyze how the expert behaved), and recombination with the current state through an MLP (Stage 3, trace back and act). The expert-state and visited-state encoders share weights.

en.text: Rolling the demonstration encoder and the context-based policy into a single architecture is what gives DDT its inductive bias toward tracing. That bias is also what lets it generalize to demonstrations - and to disturbances - it never saw during training, rather than memorizing a fixed mapping from context to action.

zh.text: 来自人类模仿的蓝本
方法的设计起点,是人类如何模仿一条路线。沿着示范路线走向目的地时,你遇到一辆停在原本没有障碍处的卡车。你不会僵住,也不会重头再来,而是绕过障碍,再在合适的地方重新汇入原路线。作者把这一过程提炼成一个三阶段决策流程:识别(identify)当前情境下哪些示范状态相关,分析(analyze)专家在这些状态下如何行动,再追踪(trace)回到示范之上。

zh.caption: 图2 未预料变化下单样本模仿的人类蓝本。专家轨迹(虚线)从起点 S 通向目标 P;一辆采集示范时并不存在的卡车挡住了状态 B。合格的模仿者会离开示范路径、绕行(绿色),再重新汇入示范——先识别、再分析、最后追踪回去。

zh.text: 这套蓝本不只是叙事上的点缀,它会直接变成网络的结构:三个阶段各自对应示范 Transformer 中一项具体运算。正是这种对应关系,把关于人类行为的直觉转化成模型可以学习的归纳偏置。

en.text: One-shot imitation learning (OSIL) asks an agent to carry out a task after watching a single demonstration. It works remarkably well when the deployment environment looks like the one where the demonstration was recorded. The trouble is that the real world rarely holds still. After a route is demonstrated, a truck can park across the path; after a grasp is shown, the object can slip out of the gripper. These are exactly the moments where a demonstration stops being a script to replay and becomes, at best, a rough guide.

Most OSIL methods embed the demonstration as a context vector and clone the demonstrated actions. In a stationary world that is enough. But once an unforeseen change pushes the agent into a state the demonstration never covered, blind replay has nothing sensible to say - and existing methods degrade sharply. This paper, presented at ICML 2024, takes that failure mode as its subject.

The authors' answer is Deep Demonstration Tracing (DDT): instead of replaying a demonstration, the agent learns to trace it. It figures out which demonstrated states are relevant right now, reads off how the expert behaved there, and steers back onto the demonstrated path after a detour. DDT pairs a purpose-built demonstration transformer with a meta-reinforcement-learning training scheme, and it holds up where prior one-shot imitation methods collapse.

en.caption: Figure 1. A pick-and-place task in Meta-World where the object slips mid-execution. Given the demonstration (a), a traditional OSIL policy (b) drops the object and fails, while the DDT policy (c) re-picks the object and still succeeds - the difference between replaying actions and tracing intent.

zh.title: ICML 2024 | 单条示范不该照抄,而该被“追踪”
zh.subtitle: 南京大学与南栖仙策提出 Deep Demonstration Tracing(DDT):让单样本模仿在环境突变时依然稳健

en.text: VPAM: a benchmark built for unforeseen change

To test imitation under runtime change, the authors build Valet Parking Assist in Maze (VPAM), inspired by real-world valet parking. A point agent must travel from a start to a target in a maze it has never seen globally, relying only on short local views computed from eight rays over five steps. Crucially, rectangular obstacles are randomly placed on the route and often did not exist in the demonstration, so the agent cannot simply replay demonstrated actions. Eight task variants toggle whether it is a single map or many, whether obstacles appear, and whether the agent is told its own coordinates.

en.caption: Figure 4. A VPAM maze. The agent moves from the start (blue) to the target (green) guided by the demonstration points (gray), while unexpected obstacles (brown) block the demonstrated route. The agent perceives only a small local view (shaded), and DDT's imitation trajectory (red) detours around each obstacle and rejoins the demonstration.

en.text: Beyond VPAM, DDT is also evaluated on robotics benchmarks: Meta-World with added disturbances, Gymnasium's Reacher and Pusher, and a MuJoCo manipulation task involving grasping, stacking, and clutter, along with partially observable variants of the VPAM maze itself.

zh.text: VPAM:为“未预料变化”而生的基准

为了检验运行时变化下的模仿能力,作者构建了 VPAM(Valet Parking Assist in Maze,迷宫代客泊车),灵感来自现实中的代客泊车。一个质点智能体要在从未从全局见过的迷宫里,从起点走到目标,只能依靠由 8 条射线、5 步范围计算出的局部视野。关键在于,矩形障碍会随机出现在路线上,而它们往往在示范中并不存在,因此智能体无法简单照抄示范动作。八个任务变体分别切换:单张地图还是多张、是否出现障碍、以及是否提供坐标。

zh.caption: 图4 一张 VPAM 迷宫。智能体在示范点(灰色)引导下,从起点(蓝色)走向目标(绿色),而未预料的障碍(棕色)挡住了示范路线。智能体只能感知很小的局部视野(阴影区),DDT 的模仿轨迹(红色)绕过每个障碍后重新汇入示范。

zh.text: 除 VPAM 外,DDT 还在多个机器人基准上评测:带扰动的 Meta-World、Gymnasium 的 Reacher 与 Pusher,以及一个涉及抓取、堆叠与杂乱环境的 MuJoCo 操作任务,另有部分可观测的 VPAM 变体。

en.title: DDT: Teaching an Imitator to Trace, Not Replay, a Single Demonstration
en.subtitle: ICML 2024 - Nanjing University and Polixir Technologies on one-shot imitation that survives unforeseen changes

zh.title: ICML 2024 | 单条示范不该照抄,而该被“追踪”
zh.subtitle: 南京大学与南栖仙策提出 Deep Demonstration Tracing(DDT):让单样本模仿在环境突变时依然稳健

en.text: How well does it hold up?

On VPAM, DDT leads across every setting - and, more tellingly, it degrades far less as conditions get harder. Moving from the training distribution to non-obstacle test maps to unforeseen obstacles, DDT drops only from 0.86 to 0.84 to 0.73, a 15% fall. The baselines fall 20%, 33%, and 52% over the same span, so DDT retains at least 5% more of its performance than any competitor.

en.caption: Figure 5. Success rates on VPAM across three settings. DDT (red) leads DCRL, CbMRL, and the behavior-cloning Trans4OSIL in every setting, and the gap widens under unforeseen obstacles - where DDT reaches 0.73 against the best baseline's 0.57. Black bars show standard error across tasks over three seeds.
Table 1. VPAM success rates (higher is better) and degradation from Train to the Unforeseen-Obstacle setting.

en.text: The robotics results tell the same story more starkly. On Meta-World with disturbance, DDT succeeds 61% of the time on unseen demonstrations, whereas the strongest baseline manages at most about 12%. The meta-RL mechanism, not just the transformer, is what buys this robustness to change.
Ablations and scaling

Two ablations confirm that both ingredients matter. Swapping the demonstration transformer for a standard transformer noticeably lowers asymptotic performance - so it is the tailored architecture, not attention in general, that drives the imitation ability. Removing the OSIL reward and learning only from the sparse ending reward sharply slows learning, because the OSIL reward supplies the dense signal that lets the agent follow the demonstration early in training.

en.caption: Figure 8. Left: learning curves (success rate vs. environment steps) for DDT and its ablations; replacing the demonstration transformer or dropping the OSIL reward both hurt. Right: asymptotic success rate as data and model size scale up (log x-axis) - performance climbs log-linearly, with roughly a 2x gain from scaling model parameters.

en.text: The scaling curves are a quieter but intriguing result: DDT improves log-linearly with both data volume and model size, roughly doubling as parameters grow. That clean scaling behavior is what leads the authors to suggest DDT could serve as a backbone for larger, more general decision-making agents.

zh.text: 示范 Transformer

核心模块把智能体当前状态作为查询(query),把示范的状态-动作对作为键(key)与值(value)。注意力加权模块为“当前哪些示范状态重要”打分,对应识别阶段;随后的逐点相乘(point-wise multiplication)把这些权重与编码后的专家行为结合,读出专家在那些状态下做了什么,对应分析阶段;结果再与当前状态重新融合,经一个 MLP 输出动作,对应追踪阶段。专家状态编码器与已访状态编码器共享权重,使示范状态与当前状态在同一表示空间中比较。

zh.caption: 图3 示范 Transformer。自下而上,人类的三个阶段被落实为网络运算:注意力加权(阶段一,识别该跟随哪些状态)、逐点相乘(阶段二,分析专家如何行动),以及与当前状态重新融合后经 MLP 输出动作(阶段三,追踪回去并行动)。专家状态编码器与已访状态编码器共享权重。

zh.text: 把示范编码器与基于上下文的策略整合进同一个架构,正是 DDT 倾向“追踪”的归纳偏置来源。也正是这种偏置,让它能够泛化到训练中从未见过的示范与扰动,而不是死记一套从上下文到动作的固定映射。
消融与规模化
两项消融确认了两个要素缺一不可。把示范 Transformer 换成标准 Transformer,渐近性能明显下降——可见起作用的是这套量身定制的架构,而非泛泛的注意力机制。去掉 OSIL 奖励、只用稀疏的结束奖励学习,则会显著拖慢学习,因为 OSIL 奖励提供的稠密信号,正是让智能体在训练早期就能紧跟示范的关键。

zh.caption: 图8 左:DDT 及其消融版本的学习曲线(成功率对环境步数);替换示范 Transformer 或去掉 OSIL 奖励都会带来损害。右:随数据量与模型规模扩大时的渐近成功率(横轴为对数)——性能呈对数线性上升,仅扩大模型参数就带来约 2x(两倍)的提升。

zh.text: 规模化曲线是一个更安静却引人兴趣的结果:DDT 随数据量与模型规模都呈对数线性提升,参数增大时成功率大致翻倍。正是这种干净的规模化行为,让作者提出 DDT 或可作为更大、更通用决策智能体的骨干网络。

zh.text: 规模化曲线是一个更安静却引人兴趣的结果:DDT 随数据量与模型规模都呈对数线性提升,参数增大时成功率大致翻倍。正是这种干净的规模化行为,让作者提出 DDT 或可作为更大、更通用决策智能体的骨干网络。

zh.title: ICML 2024 | 单条示范不该照抄,而该被“追踪”
zh.subtitle: 南京大学与南栖仙策提出 Deep Demonstration Tracing(DDT):让单样本模仿在环境突变时依然稳健

en.text: How well does it hold up?

On VPAM, DDT leads across every setting - and, more tellingly, it degrades far less as conditions get harder. Moving from the training distribution to non-obstacle test maps to unforeseen obstacles, DDT drops only from 0.86 to 0.84 to 0.73, a 15% fall. The baselines fall 20%, 33%, and 52% over the same span, so DDT retains at least 5% more of its performance than any competitor.

en.caption: Figure 5. Success rates on VPAM across three settings. DDT (red) leads DCRL, CbMRL, and the behavior-cloning Trans4OSIL in every setting, and the gap widens under unforeseen obstacles - where DDT reaches 0.73 against the best baseline's 0.57. Black bars show standard error across tasks over three seeds.
Table 1. VPAM success rates (higher is better) and degradation from Train to the Unforeseen-Obstacle setting.

en.text: The robotics results tell the same story more starkly. On Meta-World with disturbance, DDT succeeds 61% of the time on unseen demonstrations, whereas the strongest baseline manages at most about 12%. The meta-RL mechanism, not just the transformer, is what buys this robustness to change.

zh.text: 它真的在“追踪”吗?
一个以“追踪”命名的方法,理应证明它确实在追踪。作者把 DDT 在迷宫中的一次运行,与示范 Transformer 在智能体前进时对专家轨迹给出的注意力分数一并可视化。如果 DDT 确实在跟随示范,那么注意力应当大致随智能体自身的推进,沿着专家路径逐步移动。

zh.caption: 图7 左:DDT 生成的一条轨迹,绕过障碍后重新回到示范路线。右:注意力分数图,纵轴为智能体步数,横轴为专家步数。明亮的条带沿对角线延伸——智能体每前进一步,注意力就跟踪到示范的对应部分,这正是“追踪”的可视化。

zh.text: 那条对角线正是机制如预期般工作的证据:注意力随智能体同步跟随示范,恰在需要绕行时短暂偏离,绕行之后又重新锁定。这是一个令人安心的验证,说明架构确实在做它被设计去鼓励的那件事。

en.caption: Figure 1. A pick-and-place task in Meta-World where the object slips mid-execution. Given the demonstration (a), a traditional OSIL policy (b) drops the object and fails, while the DDT policy (c) re-picks the object and still succeeds - the difference between replaying actions and tracing intent.

en.text: Takeaway

The core idea is small and durable: an agent handed a single demonstration should learn to trace it, not replay it - identifying which demonstrated states are relevant now, reading off what the expert did, and steering back onto the path after a detour. DDT operationalizes this with a demonstration transformer trained by meta-RL, and the payoff is one-shot imitation that stays robust when the environment changes at runtime, a regime where earlier methods fail.

The honest boundaries are worth keeping in view: the single-demonstration guarantee rests on a recoverability condition, and the headline results live on a purpose-built maze benchmark alongside a set of robotics tasks. Within that scope, though, DDT is a clean demonstration that the right inductive bias plus reinforcement learning beats behavior cloning when the world refuses to stay still - and its scaling behavior hints at more to come.
